rationale_bullets: Layne is a real 13-start returning starter: 438 snaps, 73.1 -> 65.8 MWC-adj; 2,486 @ 65%, 13-10 - and 10 of the 13 INTs came in three games.
He was LIMITED IN SPRING and both prints call the Moga battle live - the Oregon ex-4-star (10.4 100m) is a genuine challenger, plus waiver-year runner Laubstein (override).
Team PASS was p71 - the passing offense worked.
34 = second-best QB room of the G5 rounds after WMU's 46; above Miami 30, below CMU 38/EMU 40 on tape depth.

Top two 2025 backs gone (Bankston expired, McKinney -> Tulsa); Humphrey returns with modest tape here (63.1/78) but real pedigree volume (Montana St '24: 1,386 @ 7.0) and an injury excuse (Wk 3, never recovered).
FBS depth: Sibley (NTU 274 @ 6.1 - the resolved no-dest ghost), Buchanan (Idaho 567 @ 7.2 in '24), Mathews (Memphis rFr, two-sided miss).
16 = SJSU/Buffalo tier; a healthy Humphrey is the upside case.
Omeire's import tape (69.8/236 -> 66.1 adj; 31-514-5 at UNLV) out-grades both departed leaders - a rare G5 case of upgrading through the portal.
Keith (70.3 -> 66.6) is an All-MWC candidate TE in a TE-emphasis offense; Miller (BOLD) and Z.Smith add returning route volume at low grades.
M.Williams (EWash 12 st, 524 - feed-gap) projected WR2; USC TE Olsen + ISU TE Walsh depth.
22 = Buffalo tier: real producers, no elite one.
data_gaps: Miller's grade is poor for a starter

rationale_bullets: Four returning starters with 52 combined 2025 starts - the most of the MWC round: Robnett (2nd-Tm MWC C, 865 snaps), Tasi (72.6 raw - the best adj grade at 62.5), Aliane (13 st), Lawrence (13 st).
LT goes to Weber St import Millward (12 st - feed-gap); Temple's Meir + JC Fetcho depth.
PBLK was p19 as-played - the pass-pro must improve for the passing offense to hold.
24: edges Nevada 22 on count/continuity; below CMU/WMU 28.
James-Newby (88.8/683, 7th-round pick PHI) + Karhu (587) + Lopez (468) leave - the p94 pass rush loses its engine.
But the retained rotation is real: Agu (79.2/392 -> 77.0 adj - 'big season' per both prints), Booker (73.0/411, 3rd-Tm MWC), Slayton, McIver, + Memphis import Marable (222 snaps).
PS: 'DT is the strength... DE may be the biggest question mark.'
22 = KSU tier; below Nevada 26 (no LaBarbera-class piece), above Toledo/WMU 18.
Eck is the reigning MWC DEFENSIVE PLAYER OF THE YEAR: 83.0 on 759 snaps (78.3 adj), 129 tackles, 1st-Tm MWC - 'truly the heartbeat of that defense' (opposing coach).
Swaim (77.3/402 -> 72.6) is an All-MWC candidate running mate - the best returning LB DUO of the G5 rounds, in a scheme built around them.
Exceeds the UNLV-40 anchor's profile (their leader: 73.9/808); depth behind the duo is thin (Boise's Martineau + rFr/FR).
44 = new G5-round LB high; capped below 50 by the two-deep.
data_gaps: two-deep after the duo is unproven

rationale_bullets: Six returning 300+ snap bodies at 61-74 adj: McBean (true-So BOLD), Combs (38 career starts, yr4 override), Edwards, Brawley (74.1, override, back from OFY), Speech, A.Williams - the most returning DB volume of the MWC round.
Loses its best corner (Jon Johnson 75.4/766) and Coleman; imports Arnold (Cincy), McClain (Ball St), Hicks (Hampton 12 st) restock CB.
PDR rose to #111 despite injuries; PS: 'should make a solid unit.'
26 = Miami tier; > Nevada/KSU 18, < EMU 28/WMU 30.
ALL FOUR specialists from a top-25 unit are gone (P Hughes 45.9/43.6 -> Florida State; K 15-16; KR Bankston; PR McKinney).

The rebuild has pedigree: P Kern (PS#3; Texas + Cal history) vs incumbent Steinkamp (split print); K three-way led by Romero (Wagner 13-14, FCS Frosh AA); KR A.Williams (5 career KO-return TDs at Weber St - elite history).
18 = NIU/BGSU tier: pedigree without 2025 production in these jobs.
